subtopics.title: Program structure, compiling and data types
subtopics.theory_md:
A C program is `#include <stdio.h>`, then `int main(void) { declarations; statements; return 0; }`. Every statement ends with `;`, and every variable is declared before use.

**Build steps:** source `.c` -> preprocessor (`#include`, `#define`) -> compiler (object code) -> **linker** (adds library code such as `printf`) -> executable. With gcc: `gcc prog.c -o prog`, run `./prog`. Syntax errors appear at compile time; logic errors only when you run.

**Types and formats:** `char` 1 byte (`%c`, signed range -128 to 127, wraps), `int` 4 bytes (`%d`), `float` 4 bytes (`%f`), `double` 8 bytes (`%lf` in scanf). `scanf` needs the address: `scanf("%d", &n);`. Extra `printf` arguments are ignored.

subtopics.title: Digit extraction, swapping and bitwise operators
subtopics.theory_md:
**Digits:** `n % 10` is the last digit, `n / 10` removes it. 3-digit number: units `n % 10`, tens `(n/10) % 10`, hundreds `n / 100`.

- Comma operator returns its last operand: `z = (b, a)` gives `a`.

subtopics.title: Logical operators and short-circuit evaluation
subtopics.theory_md:
`&&` (AND), `||` (OR), `!` (NOT) work on truth values: 0 is false, any non-zero is true, and the result is always 1 or 0. Precedence: `!` > `&&` > `||`.

- `A && B`: if A is false, B is **not evaluated**.
- `A || B`: if A is true, B is **not evaluated**.

subtopics.title: switch statement and fall-through
subtopics.theory_md:
```c
switch (expr) { case 1: ...; break; case 2: case 3: ...; break; default: ...; }
```
- `expr` must be an integer or char; `case` labels are distinct integer/char **constants** (no ranges, floats or variables).
- Control jumps to the matching label and then runs on **through all following cases** until a `break`: this is **fall-through**. Without `break` in a case, the next case's code also runs.
- `default` runs if nothing matches; it can sit anywhere, and falls through if it has no `break`.
- Statements placed before the first `case` are never executed.
- Grouped labels share code: `case 1: case 3: case 5: days = 31; break;`
- The expression is evaluated once; `switch (a > b)` has only cases 0 and 1.
subtopics.basics_md: A switch is a menu: the value picks a line to jump to, and the computer then keeps reading downwards until it meets a break.

subtopics.title: Solving without relational operators
subtopics.theory_md:
Papers ask for tests "without `<`, `>`, `==`" or "without `%`". The tools:

- **Non-zero is true:** `if (a - b)` means a is not equal to b; `if (a ^ b)` is the same via XOR.
- **Sign bit:** for a 32-bit int, `(unsigned)n >> 31` is 1 for negative, 0 otherwise.
- **Parity:** `n & 1` is 1 for odd, 0 for even.
- **Formula:** $\max(a,b) = \dfrac{a+b+|a-b|}{2}$, $\min(a,b) = \dfrac{a+b-|a-b|}{2}$ (`abs()` from `<stdlib.h>`).
- **Mask select:** `mask = (a - b) >> 31` is all 1s if a < b, else 0; `max = (b & mask) | (a & ~mask)`.
- **Quotient trick:** `switch (n / 10)` tests the range 10 to 99 using case 1 to case 9.
- Characters: `!(c1 - c2)` is 1 when equal.

A recursive function calls itself on a smaller problem and stops at a **base case**. Each call gets its own variables on the stack.

subtopics.title: Unions and space-efficient structures
subtopics.theory_md:
A **union** is declared like a structure, but all members **share the same memory**:
```c
union data { int i; float f; char c; };
```
- Its size is the size of its **largest member**; a structure's size is the sum of its members (plus padding).
- Only the member written last holds a valid value.
- Use a union when only one of several alternatives is needed at a time, to save memory.
- **Space-efficient record:** keep the common members in a structure and put the alternatives in a union, with a tag to remember which one is valid:
```c
struct item { int id; char color; int type;
              union { int ram; float eer; } u; };
```
Members are accessed with the dot operator as usual.
subtopics.basics_md: A structure gives every fact its own shelf. A union has a single shelf that different facts take turns using, so it is small but holds only one at a time.
key_points: Union members share one memory location
Union size = size of the largest member
Only the last written member is valid
Use when only one alternative is needed at a time
